reviewContext.issueReference: workflow-input:Complete Work Runtime P1 using the accepted dispatcher, guard, and director design
reviewContext.userProblem: Complete every unchecked Work Runtime P1 task using the accepted dispatcher, guard, director, reservation, capability-placement, CLI, example, documentation, and verification design while retaining correct stopped-workflow changes and preserving unrelated work.
requiredOutcomes: Implement P1-0 through P1-8 with atomic attempt and WorkflowSession reservation, one-live-attempt fencing, one-use launch authorization, and durable cancellation and rerun/recovery requests.

Persist typed guard evidence before deterministic, agent, or human decisions; enforce total ordered direction, completion reconstruction, causal evidence, optimistic concurrency, and idempotent decision replay.
Resolve reachable-node requirements, merge host capability evidence, place work deterministically before reservation, and expose host-aware doctor, workflow usage, and validation behavior.
Ship task run, side-effect-free dry-run, task decide, bounded agent-director execution, and equivalent dispatcher coverage before removing workflow auto-improve behavior.

Replace obsolete examples, reconcile documentation/help/surface catalogs, audit package digests, preserve P0, and close with complete foreground verification plus independent adversarial and combined-tree review with no open high or mid finding.
nonGoals: Do not implement P2 loop-store folding, P3 routine/specialist/event migration or task serve, P4 repository worktree/finalization migration, P5 GraphQL task/host APIs or GUI, P6 workflow-change proposals, or P7 capability ceilings.

Do not add Jujutsu support, a new planner, remote principal authentication, specialist classification, recursive director repair, migration or compatibility for removed auto-improve state, or implicit task creation for plain workflow run.
Do not use the canonical project-scope workflow as an implementation dependency.
constraints: Execute implementation and review only through the installed user-scope codex-design-and-implement-review-loop package on the same branch and working directory.
Do not push, integrate, create implementation worktrees, or modify Monja-owned or separate Tauri worktrees without separate authorization.
Preserve correct in-scope stopped-workflow edits and all unrelated tracked, untracked, and staged state; never reset, clean, stage all files, or overwrite from stale buffers.
Keep scratch evidence under tmp/, run commands in the foreground, poll yielded sessions through terminal exit, and retain final exit status plus complete log path.
Workers edit only their plan-owned progress file; lockfiles, shared indexes, global plan archiving, digest refresh, broad formatting, and cross-plan repair are serial reconciliation work.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Reservation is the commit point so task version, dependency checks, attempt, unique session snapshot, lease, decision/request, placement evidence, and task advancement either commit together or roll back together.
TaskDispatcher owns orchestration while the existing workflow runner owns execution, preserving the RielaCore-to-RielaWork dependency boundary.
Guard evaluation consumes a snapshot and persists the whole violation batch before direction, providing replay-safe causal evidence.
The deterministic director uses budget, convergence, inactivity, recoverable failure or gate rejection, completion, then wait-human ordering so one snapshot yields one stable decision.
Human, policy, and agent decisions share one store-backed applier so completion, causality, task-version, cancellation, and replay rules cannot diverge.
Placement uses one reachable-node requirement projection and one merged capability snapshot before reservation, preventing unreachable nodes or stale validation from authorizing execution.
Auto-improve is removed in the same delivery cut only after the dispatcher has equivalent inactivity, bounded retry, recovery, cancellation, and replay coverage.
intentionalTradeoffs: Explicit backend enablement may remain usable but unverified after an absent or failed probe; the failure remains visible and never becomes authenticated evidence.

Same-directory parallelism is retained for dependency-ready plans, with immutable intent records, pre-write drift checks, runtime change evidence, serial repair, and independent combined-tree review controlling overwrite risk.
Host validation is read-only and advisory unless strict-host is requested; dispatch independently refreshes and re-evaluates placement before reservation.
No browser E2E gate is required because P1 plans no web changes.
supportedEdgeCases: Independent-connection reservation races, rollback at transactional insertion boundaries, stale task versions, missing versus unmet dependencies, duplicate attempt/session IDs, and terminal-but-unreconciled fencing.
Wrong, replayed, replaced, or uncertain launch tokens; pre- and post-authorization crashes; stale terminal writers; pending rerun/recover replay; and cancellation acknowledgment loss.
Simultaneous guard violations, exact budget and time boundaries, last-permitted-attempt completion, replay deduplication, repeated-finding fingerprints, and official SDK heartbeat exemption.

Pin-versus-policy validation, ordered fallback, unknown or stale capabilities, failed refresh, worker groups, explicit assignments, unavailable capacity, called-workflow cycles, unreachable nodes, and unknown model support.
Dry-run against absent, incompatible, or corrupt stores/configuration without creating, migrating, quarantining, caching, or mutating state; decision replay conflicts and interrupted task execution.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Migration of legacy loop, routine, specialist, event, supervision, or auto-improve records.
Repository-context worktree creation, commit/push finalization, GraphQL task/host mutations, Studio or Task-board UI, proposal/replan machinery, and capability ceilings.
Live agent credentials as a deterministic verification prerequisite and backend prompt translation or behavioral-equivalence guarantees.
residualRisks: The foreground author-check rerun completed all assertions but could not rewrite its result file under the read-only Step 5 sandbox; the existing complete exit-0 log and independently matching plan hashes support acceptance.
Same-directory race risk remains and must be controlled by immutable intent records, drift checks, serial repair, rerun regressions, and independent combined-tree review.

Validate the canonical bundle as an artifact without executing the project-scope workflow, and record the owning-package manifest audit without editing the installed package.
Build, the positive-count ImplementationWorkflowSandboxTests suite, strict touched-file lint, and diff check pass with complete foreground logs.

acceptanceCriteria: P1-1a: preserve the shared runtime-records database, schema-generation policy, P0 behavior, and RielaWork-to-RielaCore dependency direction while adding only required reservation, lease, cancellation, and pending-request storage.

P1-1b: reserveAttempt is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that atomically validates task/dependencies/budget/fence, inserts unique attempt and created session, lease, decision or request, placement evidence, and task advancement, with full rollback on injected failure.
P1-1c: one-use opaque launch tokens are digest-only and bound to the exact attempt/session; wrong, replayed, replaced, or uncertain authorization and stale terminal writers fail closed.
P1-1d: rerun/recover requests are durable and consumed once, while cancellation retains the live fence until durable runner terminal acknowledgment.
Independent-connection race, rollback, stale-version, dependency, duplicate-ID, token, crash-window, live-fence, last-attempt, replay, cancellation, P0 store, and projector tests pass.

acceptanceCriteria: P1-6a: resolve task plan, selected entry, dependencies, and refreshed placement before atomic reservation; execute exactly the reserved session ID; project terminal evidence before guard/completion and apply all decisions through the shared applier.
